PC: Ask patient a question. No response. Examine airway, note no obstruction.  *State, “Airway patent”*
Listen to bilateral lung fields and **note absence of breath sounds on the right and tracheal deviation to the left.**  *State, “absent breath sounds on the right”*

Feel femoral pulses. (If patient-actor, the participant need only state that (s)he will palpate femoral pulse.)  *State, “2+ femoral pulses”.*  Obtain heart rate and blood pressure from nurse/tech.  *State, “Heart rate and blood pressure within normal limits for age”*
Ask patient name, place and date.  *State, “Alert and oriented to person, place and time”*  Observe for spontaneous eye opening, verbal response and motor response.  *State, “GCS 14”*

Remove all clothing. (If patient-actor, the participant need only state that (s)he will remove all clothing.) Observe **bruise to R chest** and **needle from needle decompression**.  *State, “Bruise to right chest wall and needle from needle decompression”*
Inspect and palpate scalp to assess for tenderness, wounds, hematomas, or step-offs.  *State, “Atraumatic without tenderness”*
Inspect for wounds, swelling or ecchymosis and palpate for tenderness or step-offs  *State, “No trauma, no tenderness, no bruises “*
Use light to evaluate pupil size and reactivity.  *State, “Pupils equal, round and reactive to light – 4mm to 2mm bilaterally”*
Use otoscope bilaterally to evaluate for hemotympanum or bleeding of external auditory canal.  *State, “No hemotympanum bilaterally”*
Use otoscope bilaterally to evaluate for septal hematoma, bleeding to swelling.  *State, “No deformities, epistaxis or nasal septal hematoma”*
Use light to evaluate for wounds, dental trauma. Ask the patient to bite down and describe if teeth align normally.  *State, “No bleeding or malocclusion. Teeth intact.”*

Palpate anterior neck for edema, swelling, and position of the trachea. **Trachea no longer deviated.**  *State, “Trachea midline”.*  Hold C-spine in place while palpating each posterior vertebral spine.  *State, “No midline C-spine tenderness or step-offs”*

Inspect chest wall for deformity, ecchymosis or wounds. Observe **needle in anterior chest wall**, chest rise during breathing for symmetry. Palpate anterior chest wall for tenderness or crepitus. (If patient-actor, the participant need only state that (s)he will perform these steps).  *State, “Symmetric chest rise, no clavicular deformity or tenderness, no crepitus, no tenderness to palpation. ”*

Inspect abdomen for deformity, ecchymosis or wounds. Palpate in all 4 quadrants for tenderness. (If patient-actor, the participant need only state that (s)he will perform these steps).  *State, “No bruising, ecchymosis, seatbelt sign; no tenderness”*

Inspect for ecchymosis, deformity, asymmetry, or wounds. Palpate the pelvis for tenderness, Assess for mobility by compressing iliac crests gently. Inspect urethral meatus for blood. (If patient-actor, the participant need only state that (s)he will perform these steps).  *State, “Pelvis stable, no blood at the meatus, no perineal bruising or lacerations”*
Inspect for ecchymosis, deformity, asymmetry or wounds. Palpate along spine for tenderness or step-offs.  *State, “No bruising, nontender without step-offs. Good gluteal tone”*

For each extremity: Inspect for ecchymosis, deformity, or wounds. Palpate for tenderness.  *State, “No bruising, lacerations, deformities; no tenderness to upper and lower extremities.”*  For each extremity: Assess strength and sensation.  *State, “Strength 5/5 in upper and lower extremities bilaterally; sensation 5/5 in upper and lower extremities bilaterally”*  For each extremity: Assess range of motion of all joints  *State, “Full range of motion in all extremities”*
MK: State that needle decompression is required
SBP: State need for chest tube and that trauma surgery is preparing for that procedure
